exposure: BMI categories (normal weight, overweight, obese type 1, obese type 2, obese type 3)
cohort: 400 pregnant women, with 200 having a BMI > 25 and 200 having a normal BMI (18-24.9) as a control group.
finding: High maternal BMI at booking was associated with an increased risk of gestational hypertension, pre-eclampsia, GDM, shoulder dystocia, cesarean section, induced labor, and macrosomia, while it was associated with a decreased incidence of VBAC.
